# Proposing a change to a quality gate

Publish a gate-only change to `feat/gates` based on `feat/enterprise-ui`. GitHub Actions opens one pull request for this branch, or reuses the existing one. Reviewers can see the complete proposal in its **Files changed** tab. The owner reviews the exact diff, checks the evidence at the latest commit and submits an **Approve** review. A push changing the diff dismisses that approval. The existing test, performance, accessibility and packaging requirements still apply.

Product changes go on product branches. Gate controls are the anchored paths in [.github/CODEOWNERS](CODEOWNERS). This includes the workflow itself, hooks, central verification scripts, the Android benchmark and measurement settings, and the web performance and default package-size limits. Family source, documentation and ordinary family tests can go through the product flow. A mixed diff fails the path check. The unit, browser and visual matrices under `tests/acceptance/` and the per-entry `tests/packaging/bundle-baseline.json` are generated from manifests. Product changes may add test registrations or lower an existing byte limit. Removing an existing case or engine, deleting a budget, or raising it needs a gate proposal. A gate proposal updating these generated files or just the `cases` and `budgets` of a family manifest must also change an owner-covered control. Record the decision in an owned file under `.github/` when no other control changes. The existing manifest generator and packed checks verify that declared registrations match the product. Ordinary family fixtures, individual test bodies and screenshots stay with their family.

The API-depth registry is generated from family manifests. A product proposal can add bindings or register a family. The enterprise branch’s serializer must reproduce the exact Git blob, and all earlier contracts, expected behavior, evidence and bindings must survive. Only this JSON file has an ownerless literal rule inside the policy directory. The generator, its schema and the path checker remain owner-reviewed.

If a new gate must live outside an already-owned directory, first approve an ownership change for its path.

## Owner setup

1. On the enterprise branch, require pull requests, require code-owner reviews, dismiss stale approvals when the diff changes, enforce the rules for administrators, and keep the existing required `verify` and `frozen` checks. Keep global required approvals at zero if the repository allows code-owner reviews independently. Test the combination using unowned product files and a gate file before relying on it. If GitHub requires at least one general approval, retain effective protection and document that product PRs also need a reviewer. Leave the release and default branch rules in place.
2. Keep the repository’s default Actions token read-only and enable **Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests**. The proposal job requests pull-request write and contents read on pushes to this repository’s `feat/gates` only. It uses fixed head and base branches and neither checks out nor executes submitted code. The job only opens a PR. GitHub’s native base-branch CODEOWNERS requirement reserves gate approval for `@thetechgeeek`. Treat write access to the proposal branch as trusted publishing access. Keep the owner’s review credentials under human control.
3. If the owner is also the only publisher for workflow files, leave **Require approval of the most recent reviewable push** off. Otherwise that owner cannot approve their own push. Dismissing stale reviews protects the latest diff. A separately authenticated publisher and human reviewer can use both settings. GitHub does not let a PR author approve their own PR.
4. Bootstrap by publishing this governance-only proposal to `feat/gates` and enabling the owner review requirement before merging. The previous enterprise CODEOWNERS file already assigns all paths to the owner. The first path check accepts only the five governance files in this proposal. Subsequent checks load the path checker and ownership list from the captured enterprise base. The branch push starts the proposal workflow even when default `main` is still the initial commit. Review and approve any GitHub prompt to run workflows for the bot’s PR, then wait for the required results and submit the separate human review.
5. Verify on GitHub that a product-only PR passes the path check, a product PR changing the Android limit fails, a mixed gate PR fails, and a gate-only PR remains **Review required** until the human owner approves. Verify that a new reviewable push dismisses that approval. The read-only `frozen` job also runs the proposed routing tests. A push to the landed enterprise commit emits its own receipt; main continues to receive a push receipt when it contains this workflow. The `frozen` status reports file routing and its tests. GitHub branch protection supplies the approval requirement.

GitHub documents [base-branch code ownership](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners) and [protected branch review requirements](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches).
